questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: The adrenal cortex constitutes what percentage of the adrenal gland?
questions.exp: The adrenal gland is 80% cortex and 20% medulla, situated on the kidney. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: The fetal : adult adrenal ratio is:
questions.exp: Fetal : adult adrenal ratio is 4:1. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: The adrenal primordium arises from:
questions.exp: At 6 weeks the urogenital ridge (a mesodermal derivative) gives the adrenal primordium (coelomic epithelium). (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: Hormone synthesis in the developing adrenal begins at:
questions.exp: Hormone synthesis starts at 8 weeks of intra-uterine life. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: Urine formation begins at:
questions.exp: Note: urine formation begins at 9–10 weeks. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: Adrenal development is completed by:
questions.exp: Development is completed at 12 weeks; kidney development completes at 32–36 weeks. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: Kidney development is completed between:
questions.exp: Kidney development is completed by 32–36 weeks. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: The transcription factors listed for adrenal development are:
questions.exp: Transcription factors: SF-1, DAX1 (orphan receptors), WNT4. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: Match the suprarenal artery to its origin — 1) Superior suprarenal  2) Middle suprarenal  3) Inferior suprarenal … A) Direct branch of aorta  B) Renal artery branch  C) Inferior phrenic artery branch
questions.exp: Superior suprarenal = inferior phrenic branch; middle = direct aortic branch; inferior = renal artery branch. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Adrenal cortex: anatomy, embryology and blood supply · p837
questions.q: Match adrenal venous drainage — 1) Right adrenal vein  2) Left adrenal vein … A) Drains to left renal vein, then IVC  B) Drains directly to IVC
questions.exp: Right adrenal vein drains straight to the IVC; left adrenal vein drains to the left renal vein, then IVC. (Book p837)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: Match adrenal relations — 1) Right gland anterior  2) Right gland posterior  3) Left gland anterior  4) Left gland posterior … A) Right crus of diaphragm  B) Stomach, pancreas, spleen  C) IVC and right liver lobe  D) Left crus of diaphragm
questions.exp: Right anterior: IVC + right liver lobe; right posterior: right crus; left anterior: stomach, pancreas, spleen; left posterior: left crus. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: The principal hormone of the fetal zone is:
questions.exp: The fetal zone's principal hormone in fetal life is DHEAS; the zone regresses after birth. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: ‘The fetal zone of the adrenal cortex persists and enlarges after birth.’
opts: True — it becomes the zona fasciculata
questions.exp: The fetal zone regresses after birth. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: Match definitive zone to hormone and regulator — 1) Zona glomerulosa  2) Zona fasciculata  3) Zona reticularis … A) Cortisol, pituitary  B) DHEAS, pituitary  C) Aldosterone, RAAS
questions.exp: ZG → aldosterone under RAAS; ZF → cortisol under pituitary; ZR → DHEAS under pituitary. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: The zona fasciculata contributes what share of the cortex?
questions.exp: Contributions: ZG 15%, ZF 75%, ZR 10%. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: Match zone to cortical contribution — 1) Zona glomerulosa  2) Zona fasciculata  3) Zona reticularis … A) 10%  B) 15%  C) 75%

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: The zona reticularis forms by ___ of age (unlike the other zones, present at birth).
questions.exp: ZG and ZF are formed at birth; ZR forms by 2–3 years. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: Adrenarche — pubic and axillary hair growth from the zona reticularis — begins at:
questions.exp: Adrenarche occurs at 6–8 years and regresses post reproductive age. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: Maximum daily DHEAS production by the zona reticularis exceeds:
questions.exp: DHEAS is produced max daily >20 mg by the zona reticularis. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Relations, fetal zone and definitive zone · p838
questions.q: On histology, the ‘large lipid-rich clear cells’ belong to the:
questions.exp: The zona fasciculata shows large lipid-rich clear cells. (Book p838)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: StAR stands for ___, the rate-limiting step of steroid synthesis.
questions.exp: StAR = steroid acute regulatory protein; it is the rate-limiting step and its defect causes congenital lipid hyperplasia. (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: StAR catalyses the first step, converting:
questions.exp: Cholesterol (LDL) enters via StAR to form pregnenolone. (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: A neonate with pan-steroid deficiency is found to have a StAR defect. The named condition is:
questions.exp: The StAR defect (rate-limiting step) causes congenital lipid hyperplasia. (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: Match the 17α-hydroxylase conversions — 1) Pregnenolone  2) Progesterone … A) 17OH-progesterone  B) 17OH-pregnenolone
questions.exp: 17α-hydroxylase converts pregnenolone→17OH-pregnenolone and progesterone→17OH-progesterone. (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: 17,20 lyase converts 17OH-pregnenolone to:
questions.exp: 17,20 lyase yields dehydroepiandrosterone from 17OH-pregnenolone (and androstenedione from 17OH-progesterone). (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase converts pregnenolone to:
questions.exp: 3β-HSD converts pregnenolone→progesterone (and the 17OH pair likewise). (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: Match the 21α-hydroxylase substrates/products — 1) Progesterone  2) 17OH-progesterone … A) 11-Deoxycortisol  B) Deoxycorticosterone
questions.exp: 21α-hydroxylase: progesterone→deoxycorticosterone; 17OH-progesterone→11-deoxycortisol. (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: Match the 11β-hydroxylase conversions — 1) Deoxycorticosterone  2) 11-Deoxycortisol … A) Cortisol  B) Corticosterone
questions.exp: 11β-hydroxylase: deoxycorticosterone→corticosterone; 11-deoxycortisol→cortisol. (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: Match the aldosterone arm — 1) Corticosterone →(18-hydroxylase)  2) 18OH-corticosterone →(aldosterone synthase) … A) Aldosterone  B) 18OH-corticosterone
questions.exp: Corticosterone→18OH-corticosterone (18-hydroxylase) then →aldosterone (aldosterone synthase). (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: Which enzymes are present ONLY in the zona glomerulosa?
questions.exp: The 18-hydroxylase/aldosterone synthase arm is only in ZG, explaining zone-specific aldosterone. (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: Match gonadal enzymes — 1) Androstenedione→testosterone  2) Testosterone→DHT  3) Androstenedione→estrone … A) 5α-reductase type II  B) Aromatase (POR)  C) 17β-HSD type 3
questions.exp: 17β-HSD type 3 makes testosterone (and estradiol from estrone); 5α-reductase type II makes DHT (testis); aromatase (POR) makes estrone (ovary). (Book p839)

questions.sec: Aldosterone and steroid biosynthesis pathway · p839
questions.q: In the pathway, POR stands for ___.
questions.exp: POR = P450 oxidoreductase; DHT = dihydrotestosterone; StAR = steroid acute regulatory protein. (Book p839)

questions.sec: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 defects · p840
questions.q: The inherited form of 11β-OH steroid dehydrogenase type 2 defect is called:
questions.exp: Inherited 11β-HSD2 defect = apparent mineralocorticoid excess (AME). (Book p840)

questions.sec: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 defects · p840
questions.q: Normally, 11β-OH steroid dehydrogenase type 2 converts:
questions.exp: The enzyme converts cortisol (glucocorticoid + mineralocorticoid) to cortisone (glucocorticoid only). (Book p840)

questions.sec: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 defects · p840
questions.q: ‘In AME the blocked cortisol→cortisone step causes excess cortisol, which then acts as a mineralocorticoid.’
opts: True, but only with a tumour
questions.exp: Blocking the conversion leaves excess cortisol driving mineralocorticoid effects (AME). (Book p840)

questions.sec: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 defects · p840
questions.q: The acquired causes of 11β-HSD2 inhibition listed are:
questions.exp: Acquired: Cushing's disease and licorice excess (inhibits 11β-OH steroid dehydrogenase type 2). (Book p840)

questions.sec: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 defects · p840
questions.q: ‘Licorice excess produces hypertension by inhibiting 11β-OH steroid dehydrogenase type 2.’
questions.exp: Licorice excess (−) inhibits 11β-HSD2, an acquired cause of the AME picture. (Book p840)

questions.sec: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 defects · p840
questions.q: A child presents with hypertension, hypokalaemia and alkalosis with salt + water retention but low aldosterone. The shared presentation triangle points to:
questions.exp: Both inherited and acquired 11β-HSD2 defects present with salt + H2O retention → HTN, alkalosis and hypokalaemia. (Book p840)

questions.sec: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 defects · p840
questions.q: Which is NOT part of the presentation triangle of 11β-HSD2 defects?
questions.exp: The triangle is hypertension, alkalosis and hypokalaemia (with salt + water retention); hyperkalaemia is the opposite. (Book p840)

units.title: Adrenal anatomy, embryology and blood supply
units.guide: Gland = 80% cortex/20% medulla on the kidney. Embryology: 6 wks urogenital ridge (mesoderm) → adrenal primordium (coelomic epithelium); 8 wks hormone synthesis; 9–10 wks urine formation; 12 wks development complete; kidney complete 32–36 wks; fetal:adult ratio 4:1; TFs SF-1, DAX1 (orphans), WNT4. Arteries: superior (inferior phrenic), middle (aorta), inferior (renal). Veins: right → IVC; left → left renal vein → IVC.

units.title: Relations, fetal zone and the definitive zones
units.guide: Right anterior IVC + right liver lobe, posterior right crus; left anterior stomach/pancreas/spleen, posterior left crus. Fetal zone: DHEAS principal, regresses after birth. Definitive: ZG (at birth, RAAS, 15%, aldosterone), ZF (at birth, pituitary, 75%, cortisol, lipid-rich clear cells), ZR (by 2–3 y, pituitary, 10%, DHEAS >20 mg/day; adrenarche 6–8 y, regresses post-reproductive).

units.title: Steroidogenesis: the enzyme ladder and zone specificity
units.guide: Cholesterol (LDL) → pregnenolone via StAR (steroid acute regulatory protein; rate-limiting; defect → congenital lipid hyperplasia). 17α-hydroxylase on both Δ pairs; 17,20 lyase → DHEA; 3β-HSD → progesterone; 21α-hydroxylase → DOC/11-deoxycortisol; 11β-hydroxylase → corticosterone/cortisol; 18-hydroxylase then aldosterone synthase (only in ZG) → aldosterone. Gonadal: 17β-HSD3 → testosterone/estradiol; 5α-reductase II → DHT (testis); aromatase (POR = P450 oxidoreductase) → estrone (ovary).

units.title: 11β-HSD2 defects: AME and licorice
units.guide: 11β-HSD2 normally converts cortisol → cortisone. Inherited defect = AME; acquired inhibition by Cushing's disease and licorice excess. Excess cortisol acts as mineralocorticoid → salt + water retention → HTN with alkalosis and hypokalaemia.
